title: Health Services Arrive as Forest and Land Fires Approach Homes in Palangka Raya
excerpt: Health services reached around 60 residents and volunteers amid a fire approaching a residential area in Palangka Raya, Kalimantan Tengah.
seoTitle: Medical Aid as Fires Near Palangka Raya Homes - Relawan Nusantara
seoDescription: Health services reached around 60 residents and volunteers amid a fire approaching a residential area in Palangka Raya, Kalimantan Tengah.
html:
As a fire approached a residential area on Jalan Bakung Merang No. 50, Tanjung Pinang Urban Village, Pahandut District, Palangka Raya City, Kalimantan Tengah, health services were brought in to help look after residents and volunteers at the affected site on Tuesday, 13 October 2016.

The flames drawing ever closer to residents' homes caused anxiety in the community. In an emergency like this, besides facing the threat of fire, residents also need attention to their health and safety.

As part of its humanitarian response, Relawan Nusantara deployed two medical teams and two volunteers to provide health services at the site. Around 60 residents and volunteers received health checks during the activity.

Resident with Acute Asthma Receives Medical Treatment

During the health service, one resident suffered an acute asthma attack and needed immediate help. The Relawan Nusantara team gave initial treatment in line with conditions in the field, before taking the resident to RS Bhayangkara (Bhayangkara Hospital) Palangka Raya for further medical care.

The incident is a reminder that in a fire situation, attention to residents' health remains important. Smoke exposure, panic, and unsafe environmental conditions can increase the risk of health problems, especially for residents with certain medical conditions.

The Presence of Health Services Strengthens Residents

For people living near the fire site, the arrival of aid is one form of support in a worrying situation.

Fatmawati, one of the residents, expressed her appreciation for the presence of health services in the neighborhood.

“Thank you to the donors, because health services have been able to come to our neighborhood.”

Meanwhile, Muhammad Fatwa, a volunteer with Relawan Nusantara, said that residents' health and safety need to be a shared concern in every emergency.

“When a fire approaches a residential area, the situation on the ground can become very tense, and we try to give initial treatment to residents who experience health problems and make sure they receive follow-up care if needed.”

On Hand to Help in an Emergency

The presence of these health services is part of the effort to stand by the community during the fire emergency in Palangka Raya. Support is needed not only to face the threat of fire, but also to make sure residents and volunteers continue to receive attention to their health.

Through collaboration and shared care, it is hoped that people facing an emergency can obtain the help they need and feel safer while the response is under way. Share your best care now!

Luaskan Manfaat
